title: Methanol Droplet Combustion in Oxygen-Inert Environments in Microgravity
summary: 8th US National Combustion Meeting paper (2013) on more than 100 FLEX methanol tests in O2/N2, O2/N2/CO2 and O2/N2/He at 0.7 and 1 atm (O2 30% down to 12%, CO2 or He up to 70%, D0 1.5-4.5 mm). Quasi-steady theory correlates K (small droplets burn faster than predicted because of water condensation); a water-absorption model predicts flame-standoff ratios, but He mixtures sit consistently above it. Diffusive extinction diameters fall on one line versus D0 regardless of diluent; a priori activation-energy asymptotics under-predicts them unless the flame temperature is lowered to about 1700 K. LOI for methanol is about 12-13% O2.

items.claim: LOI of methanol in these diluent gases is about 12-13% O2 by volume.
items.quote: The experiments also show that the limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.

items.claim: Diffusive-extinction diameters of methanol fall on one straight line versus initial diameter irrespective of diluent; large droplets at low O2 extinguish radiatively close to the 45-degree line.
items.quote: At smaller droplet sizes, the data fall approximately along a straight line, irrespective of the diluent concentrations.

items.claim: Measured methanol flame-standoff ratios in O2/N2/He mixtures are systematically higher than the simplified water-absorption model predicts, while O2/N2/CO2 data agree better.
items.quote: The measured FSRs for O2 − N2 − He mixtures are consistently higher than the predicted values compared to the O2 − N2 − CO2 mixture data points.

items.claim: Run numbering: the paper's Run #204 (methanol, D0 2.75 mm, air at 1 atm, De 1.10 mm) matches PSI row 203 (N01M201: 2.75 mm, d_ext 1.11 mm) while PSI row 204 is a heptane test; Run #263 (2.67 mm, 21% O2/30% He/49% N2 at 0.7 atm, De 1.42 mm) matches PSI row 257 (H12M201), not PSI row 263. The paper also gives air as '20% O2 and 79% N2' where PSI row 203 lists 0.21/0.79.
items.quote: Run #204 corresponds to a methanol droplet of initial diameter 2.75 mm burning in air (20% O2 and 79% N2) at one atmospheric pressure.

notes: NTRS preprint read in full (11 pp). Run #110 matches PSI row 110 exactly; other run numbers are offset from PSI row numbers.

title: Methanol Droplet Extinction in Oxygen/Carbon-dioxide/Nitrogen Mixtures in Microgravity: Results from the International Space Station Experiments
summary: Eastern States Section paper (Oct 2011) on 54 of 104 FLEX methanol tests with in-view extinction, in O2/N2/CO2 at 0.7 and 1 atm, D0 2-4 mm. Ignition and some burning occurred at 13% O2 in N2 at 1 atm. Burning-rate constants fall with O2 and deviate strongly from quasi-steady theory at low O2; flame-standoff ratio rises as O2 falls. Extinction diameters split into a diffusive band (>=18% O2) and a radiative band near the no-burn line (<=14% O2), with critical initial diameters at 15-16% O2; CO2 favours radiative extinction. Diffusive extinction corresponds to an infinite-rate flame temperature near 1800 K in 21% O2.

items.claim: At 1 atm, all methanol droplets in >=18% O2 extinguished diffusively and all in <=14% O2 radiatively; at 15% and 16% O2 a critical initial diameter separates the two modes.
items.quote: In 18 % or more O2 all droplets exhibit diffusive extinction, and in 14 % or less O2 all exhibit radiative extinction, there being critical initial diameters separating the two limiting behaviors at the two intermediate O2 concentrations.

items.claim: Added CO2 promotes radiative extinction (higher infrared emissivity); its influence on diffusive extinction resembles that of N2.
items.quote: had more CO2 in the atmosphere, suggesting that this diluent promotes radiative extinction, as expected from its much greater infrared emissivity.

items.claim: Diffusive extinction occurs when the infinite-rate flame temperature falls to about 1800 K in 21% O2 (bounded by 1750-1800 K calculations) and below 1650 K at 18% O2.
items.quote: It may thus be concluded that diffusive extinction occurs when the infinite-rate ideal flame temperature decreases to a value not far from 1800 K in atmospheres having O2 contents of 21 %. That value decreases with dilution and is less than 1650 K at 18%.

items.claim: Radiative extinctions happen so close to the initial diameter that burning was transient and ignition-energy dependent; the authors suggest such conditions lie outside the LOI, and that water absorption can be neglected for them.
items.quote: In a sense, then, one might wish to consider these atmospheric conditions to lie outside the LOI.

items.claim: Average flame-standoff ratio of methanol increases with decreasing ambient O2 at both 0.7 and 1 atm.
items.quote: As one would expect, df/d increases with decreasing ambient oxygen mole fraction since the flame needs to move father away to meet the stoichiometric requirement.

items.claim: Ignition and some burning occurred at 13% O2 in N2 at 1 atm.
items.quote: At one atmosphere pressure, ignition and some burning were observed for an oxygen concentration of 13% with the rest being nitrogen.

items.claim: Fig. 3 is captioned as 1 atm and the text says one 1 atm test at 21% O2 had 70% CO2 and 9% N2, but every PSI row with 0.21 O2/0.09 N2/0.70 CO2 (rows 10-18) is at 1546-2320 mmHg (2.0-3.05 atm); the only methanol one with an extinction diameter is row 16 (256F009, 2072 mmHg, d0 1.66, d_ext 1.0 mm).
items.quote: In most mixtures there was more N2 than CO2, but one of the tests at 21% O2 had 70% CO2 and 9% N2.

items.claim: The paper counts 104 methanol tests by its writing (Oct 2011); the PSI table has 142 methanol rows dated before 9 Oct 2011 (157 in total). The cut-off date of the count is not stated, so this is a weak discrepancy.
items.quote: Out of these, there were 104 methanol tests of which 54 tests yielded extinction diameters where the droplet remained in the filed of view of the back-lit camera.

notes: NTRS PDF has a garbled text layer (font encoding); pages were read as images. Quotes transcribed from the page images.

title: A Numerical Study On The Extinction Characteristics Of Droplet Combustion Under Microgravity Conditions
summary: Numerical study (AIAA 2012) of methanol droplet extinction under FLEX-like CO2, He and O2 dilution: distinct diffusive and radiative extinction regimes, transition controlled by CO2, helium favouring diffusive extinction with higher burning rate.

items.claim: Model shows CO2 strongly controls the diffusive-to-radiative transition and He gives higher burning rate with diffusive extinction.
items.quote: The transition from diffusive to radiative extinction is strongly influenced by ambient carbon dioxide concentration.

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; AIAA full text paywalled. Modelling only.

title: FLEX: A Decisive Step Forward in NASA's Combustion Research Program
summary: 2012 AAS preprint overview of the CIR combustion programme and early FLEX results: 276 tests in 225 conditions, LOI determined for methanol and heptane, radiative extinction below about 14% O2, flames sustained at lower O2 than in normal gravity, the cool-flame discovery and its fire-safety implication; FLEX-2 plans.

items.claim: Below about 14% O2 methanol extinguishes radiatively rather than by water absorption.
items.quote: For oxygen concentrations approximately below 14 percent, radiative extinction was found to occur rather than extinction caused by water absorption.

items.claim: The first nine FLEX tests were engineering tests in cabin air (PSI rows 1-9, identifiers ending CAL, March-April 2009, 0.21 O2/0.79 N2 at ~760 mmHg); science test points began in May 2009 (PSI row 10 is 22 May 2009). The paper misprints the year as 2099.
items.quote: The first nine “engineering” tests used cabin air rather than specified diluent gasses.

items.claim: Cool flames may re-ignite in the hot mode; hot-flame-only safety procedures may be inadequate.
items.quote: Safety procedures based only on considerations of hot flames may be inadequate for assuring safety under all conditions.

items.claim: The MDCA radiometers did not provide useful data in early FLEX tests and were redesigned.
items.quote: The MDCA radiometer, while operating to design specification, did not provide useful data

notes: Image-only PDF (44 pp); pages 1-13 read as images. Already a source of the PSI-69 and PSI-68 records.

title: Dynamics of Water Absorption and Evaporation During Methanol Droplet Combustion in Microgravity
summary: ASGSR 2012 slides (Hicks et al.): OH* chemiluminescence images from the FLEX LLUV camera mark the transition from water absorption to water evaporation in methanol droplets; compared with Zero Gravity Facility drop tests in Ar/N2. Shows FLEX extinction diameter versus D0 at 13-21% O2 in CO2/N2 at 1 atm.

items.claim: The transition from water absorption to water evaporation during methanol burning can be identified from OH* (310 nm) flame-intensity profiles in FLEX LLUV images.
items.quote: Flame intensity measurements using OH* chemiluminescence images from the FLEX LLUV camera provide information of the water flux transition point in MeOH droplet combustion studies

items.claim: Slide 9 gives FLEX-145 as 20% O2/75% CO2/5% N2, D0 3.38 mm, Dext 1.66 mm, K 0.44; PSI row 145 (C01M201) lists 0.20 O2/0.75 N2/0.05 CO2, d0 3.33, d_ext 1.61, K 0.45. Slide 10 of the same deck gives O2 20%/N2 75%/CO2 5%, D0 = 3.3 mm, agreeing with PSI; slide 9 apparently swaps N2 and CO2. Burning-rate units are printed as m2/s (should be mm2/s).

items.claim: The partial-burning model reproduces measured cool-flame K values but not their apparent dependence on pressure or initial diameter.

items.claim: Good agreement with measured and computed cool-flame standoff ratios.
items.quote: Good agreement is found, however, with newly measured and numerically calculated flame standoff ratios in this droplet combustion supported by cool flames.

title: Cool-flame extinction during n-alkane droplet combustion in microgravity
summary: Preprint (CSSCI 2014) of the 2015 Combustion and Flame paper: n-heptane, n-octane and n-decane droplets in O2/N2/CO2 and O2/He/N2 at 0.5-1 atm, 14-25% O2. All three alkanes show hot-flame radiative extinction followed by quasi-steady cool-flame burning, with cool-flame K slightly below hot-flame K. In O2/N2 the cool-flame extinction diameter scales as [O2]^(-3/4); across diluents and pressures D_ce^2/K_c correlates with [O2]^(-3/2), as an NTC-crossover argument predicts.

items.claim: Hot/cool K for n-decane and n-octane with He substitution as in the record.
items.quote: The burning rate constants K (=dD2/dt) corresponding to the first and second stage combustion were found to be 0.41 and 0.33 mm2/s respectively.

items.claim: In O2/N2, cool-flame extinction diameters of heptane, octane and decane scale with ambient O2 molar concentration to the power -3/4.
items.quote: The cool flame extinction diameters vary as oxygen molar concentration to the power -3/4 for oxygen/nitrogen mixture.

items.claim: With CO2 or He replacing N2 and at different pressures, the residence time at extinction D_ce^2/K_c correlates with [O2] at the theoretical slope -3/2.
items.quote: Remarkably the data are reasonably well correlated, considering the number of variables involved in the experiments, and, within the appreciable scatter, the results are in agreement with the theoretical slope of -3/2.

items.claim: Cool-flame burning rates are slightly lower than hot-flame rates.
items.quote: The cool flame burning rates are slightly lower compared to the hot flame rates.

notes: Read the NTRS preprint, not the paywalled journal version. Typo in the paper: R383 is given as '14%O2 and 96%N2' (sums to 110%). The three heptane cases quoted (D0 3.91, 3.48, 2.49 mm at 1 atm) do not appear in the PSI-69 table by initial diameter, so they are probably later (FLEX-2 era) tests. For PSI-39 (CFI) this is precursor work: the -3/2 correlation is the one cited in the CFI presentations. Also listed under PSI-39, PSI-68; read once.

summary: Yu and Shaw (2014): Fourier-optics analysis of FLEX/FLEX-2 backlit droplet images for non- or lightly-sooting droplets; diffraction at the droplet edge, partial coherence and background variation bias diameter measurements; an iterative edge-finding algorithm is proposed.

title: Detailed results from the flame extinugishment experiment (FLEX) - March 2009 to December 2011
summary: NASA/TP-2015-216046: the catalogue of FLEX tests from March 2009 to December 2011 (methods, data processing, Table IX of per-test results) on which the PSI-69 table is based. No interpretation is given.

items.claim: Report catalogues burning-rate constants and extinction diameters; it is the source of the PSI table.
items.quote: Burning rate—average burning rate constant from a linear fit of the droplet diameter squared versus time from shortly after ignition to extinction

items.claim: The conclusions give initial diameters of 2-5 mm and atmospheres of O2 with N2, CO2 and mixtures, but the report's own Table IX (= PSI table) has d0 from 1.10 to 4.67 mm (26 tests below 2 mm) and 50 helium-diluted rows; Appendix A also says it covers March 2009 to December 2010 while the title and table run to December 2011.
items.quote: for methanol and n-heptane droplets with initial diameters between 2 and 5 mm.
